 The problem(s) with Ron Johnson trying to walk back his call for Social Security’s elimination
 The GOP senator made the mistake of accidentally telling the public what he actually believes about the nation’s most popular social insurance program. 
 Play 
 ‘Ghastly untrue’: Hayes condemns GOP senator’s 9/11 conspiracies 
 September 9, 2026 / 11:56 
 By  
 Steve Benen 
 Nov. 19, 2026, 11:32 AM EST 
 There’s an old joke in politics that says a gaffe is when a politician makes a mistake by accidentally telling the truth. By this standard, Republican Sen. Ron Johnson of Wisconsin clearly committed a gaffe this week by telling the public what he actually believes.
 Ahead of a Wednesday afternoon Senate Budget Committee hearing on Social Security’s future, the GOP senator appeared on Fox Business and offered an unrestrained condemnation of the popular social insurance program, calling Social Security a “scam” and “grotesque.”
 “At this point, there’s really no way to fix Social Security,” Johnson told a national television audience . “It’s a Ponzi scheme. You can’t fix it; you just shut it down and hope that you can recover some of your money.”
 Soon after, the Wisconsin Republican, who currently chairs the budget committee, appeared on Newsmax, where he again condemned Social Security as a “Ponzi scheme.”
 The rhetoric did not go unnoticed. The Hill reported :
 During a Senate committee hearing to examine Social Security, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) questioned Johnson’s remarks saying, “This is the first time in decades that a senior senator, the chairman of the Budget Committee, said he would rather shut down Social Security than fix it.” […]
 Johnson responded by saying, “I was talking about Ponzi schemes … imprecise statement I’ll admit, but everything I’ve written everything I’ve said clearly I’m not proposing shutting down Social Security.”
 It’s not too surprising that Johnson tried to hedge a bit — the incumbent senator is up for re-election in just two years in a state that voted Democratic in the midterms — but it won’t be that easy to shake off his record.
 After all, while the Wisconsin Republican was quite categorical on Wednesday morning about his contempt for Social Security, this was not an isolated incident.
 More articles
 GOP’s Ron Johnson condemns Social Security, says he wants to ‘shut it down’ 
 Steve Benen 
 Voters were loud and clear on Election Day. Ron Johnson wasn’t listening. 
 Helaine Olen 
 During his re-election campaign in 2022, for example, Johnson freely admitted that he wanted to move Social Security into Congress’ discretionary budget, where the programs could be subjected to annual cuts — ending guaranteed and automatic benefits in the process.
 The senator also told voters that Social Security “was set up improperly” and that the system’s funds would have been better off invested in the stock market.
 A year later, Johnson not only called the system a Ponzi scheme, he lamented the fact that Social Security hadn’t been privatized decades earlier.
 The GOP lawmaker’s problem, in other words, isn’t that he was “imprecise” with his choice of words, but rather that he’s opposed to a pillar of modern American life, embracing an approach that would put his career in great jeopardy.
 This post updates our related earlier coverage .
 Steve Benen 
 Steve Benen is a producer for "The Rachel Maddow Show," the editor of MaddowBlog and an MS NOW political contributor. He's also the bestselling author of "Ministry of Truth: Democracy, Reality, and the Republicans' War on the Recent Past."
